pr_body:
A ctx.actions.symlink whose output is a declare_file or declare_directory
(as opposed to a declare_symlink) has "copy" semantics, i.e., the output
artifact is indistinguishable from the referent except for its name; the
symlink is just a filesystem-level optimization to avoid an actual copy,
and is transparently resolved when collecting the action output metadata.

When the symlink points to an artifact that was built remotely and without the
bytes, we currently must download it before executing the symlink action, so
that the output metadata can be constructed from the local filesystem. This
change short-circuits the filesystem traversal by injecting output metadata,
which is identical to the input plus a pointer to the original path. This is
used by the prefetcher to avoid downloading the same files multiple times when
they're symlinked more than once.

(An alternative would have been to teach all of the RemoteActionFileSystem
methods to resolve symlinks by patching together the local and remote metadata,
but that would have resulted in an awful lot of complexity.)

Fixes #15678.
pr_title: Inject metadata when creating a filesystem symlink for a non-symlink artifact.

review_comment: Do we have the case where the tree is not entirely remote? If so, how do we handle that?
No, I don't believe this could ever occur, since two actions cannot produce the same tree artifact. So I think `!isEntirelyRemote` effectively means "is entirely local".

nit: Another option is to put a value which cannot be a correct index (e.g. -1) when it is absent. That may ironically be more than 1 byte for -1 (since varint is 1 byte for 0..127). You could reserve 0 and do index + 1, but it is a little weird.
I think using 0 and 1 is fine for what's effectively a presence bit.
Check that symlink are not created on the local file system if no local actions need them?

I think `RemoteActionFileSystemTest` is a better place to check. I've also added tests there for when the symlink points to a local artifact (in which case an actual symlink should be created in the filesystem).

I believe this is obsoleted by the fact that `RemoteActionFileSystem#createSymbolicLink` now creates the symlink on both filesystems. This seems unavoidable since `RemoteActionFileSystem` is also used in contexts where modifying the local filesystem is expected (it might be possible to move this to a different filesystem implementation, but not today).
